headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure and capacity auctions from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, potentially saving residential customers money.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (initially).
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Costs Onto Data Centers
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, measures designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's amendments weakened the original intent, particularly by removing the direct shift of capacity auction costs, though the State Corporation Commission can still determine fair share.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making this information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to increase transparency and provide credible numbers for water supply planning, with the reporting website expected to be live by January 1, 2027.

headline: Establish Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on noise, water, agriculture, and historical sites before rezoning approval to address community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Josh Thomas.
news_headline: Virginia Cracks Down on Data Center Water and Noise
news_summary: Virginia has approved new regulations, including those related to data center siting and noise limits, with the Department of Environmental Quality mandated to establish strict acoustic baseline rules for cooling systems by 2029. This legislation, including HB 153, requires impact assessments for noise, water, and other environmental factors before data center rezoning approval, addressing quality of life concerns from residents.
